cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is writing to the believers in Rome. He's just told them to pay everyone what they owe: taxes, respect, honor (Romans 13:7). Now he names the one debt they're supposed to keep on owing.

cards.question: Paul tells the believers in Rome to be indebted to no one, except to one another in ___.

cards.text: Then Paul gives the reason love is the one debt worth keeping. It has to do with the law, the commandments God gave His people.

cards.question: Paul says the one who loves his neighbor has ___ the law.

cards.text: Then Paul lists commandments: “Do not commit adultery,” “Do not murder,” “Do not steal,” “Do not covet,” and any other commandments, ALL of them, summed up in one decree. Friend, I can't even sum up my Tuesday in one sentence.

cards.question: Paul says all those commandments, and every other one, are summed up in one decree. Which one?
True or false: Paul says love does no wrong to its neighbor.

cards.text: Then Paul lands it: “Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.” Love covers all of it, and meanwhile I need three timers and a sticky note just to get ONE batch out of the oven.
Then Paul says, “And do this, understanding the occasion.” Translation: friend, take a look at the clock.

cards.question: Paul tells the believers in Rome the hour has come for them to do what?
Paul says it's time to wake up, because their ___ is nearer now than when they first believed.

cards.text: This is the alarm you DON'T snooze, friend, not even for “five more minutes.” Paul says the night is nearly over and the day has drawn near.

cards.question: With the night nearly over, Paul says to lay aside the deeds of darkness and put on what?

cards.text: Paul says to behave decently, as in the daytime. That means not in carousing and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and debauchery.

cards.question: True or false: Paul puts dissension and jealousy on the same list as drunkenness.

cards.text: Instead of all that, Paul tells them what to put on. And no, friend, it's not an apron. I checked. TWICE.

cards.question: Instead of the deeds of darkness, Paul says to clothe yourselves with whom?
True or false: Paul says to leave a little room for the desires of the flesh, just in case.

findings.problem: This is a cloze of Romans 13:8 rather than a meaning the baker can reason out. Card 1 says only that one debt remains; it gives no basis for choosing love over gratitude or labor.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This blanks the wording of Romans 13:8 without enough setup to reason out the answer. Card 3 says only that the reason has to do with the law, leaving the baker to guess fulfilled rather than replaced or outgrown.
